_note: Mock data for the Practice your mistakes cabinet.

cards.front: A block rests on a 30° incline. A student writes N = mg. What did they miss?
cards.back: The normal force only balances the part of gravity that pushes into the surface: N = mg cos 30° ≈ 0.87 mg. Writing mg overstates it by about 15%.

cards.front: Which part of the weight pulls the block down the slope?
cards.back: mg sin θ, along the slope. The other part, mg cos θ, presses into the surface and is the one the normal force cancels.

mistakes.title: Friction left out of the net force

cards.front: A box is pushed with 40 N across a floor; kinetic friction is 12 N. A student uses 40 N for the net force. What is wrong?
cards.back: Friction acts against the motion, so the net force is 40 N − 12 N = 28 N. Use the net force in F = ma, not the applied force.

cards.front: Which way does kinetic friction point?
cards.back: Opposite to the direction the surfaces slide past each other, whatever direction the push is.

cards.front: Two resistors are in series. A student says the current is larger through the smaller one. Why is that wrong?
cards.back: A series circuit has one path, so the same current flows through every part of it. The smaller resistor has a smaller voltage across it, not a larger current.

cards.front: 0.50 mol of water. A student divides by 18 g/mol to get grams. What went wrong?
cards.back: Going from moles to grams, multiply by the molar mass: 0.50 mol × 18 g/mol = 9.0 g. Divide only when going from grams to moles.

cards.front: How can the units tell you whether to multiply or divide?
cards.back: Write the units in. mol × g/mol leaves grams; mol ÷ g/mol leaves mol²/g, which is not a mass.

cards.front: A student uses 16 g/mol for oxygen gas. Why is the answer off by a factor of 2?
cards.back: Oxygen gas is O₂, so its molar mass is 2 × 16 = 32 g/mol.

cards.front: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O with 3 mol H₂ and 2 mol O₂. A student picks O₂ as limiting because there is less of it. Check it.
cards.back: Compare against the ratio. 3 mol H₂ needs 1.5 mol O₂, and there are 2 mol, so H₂ runs out first. H₂ is limiting.

cards.front: A student reads codons straight off the DNA template strand. What should they read instead?
cards.back: Transcribe first. The mRNA is complementary to the template, with U in place of T, and codons are read from the mRNA, 5′ to 3′.

cards.front: Template 3′-TAC-5′. What is the mRNA codon?
cards.back: 5′-AUG-3′, the start codon, which codes for methionine.

cards.front: mRNA: AUG GCU UAA GGC. A student lists four amino acids. How many are there?
cards.back: Two. UAA is a stop codon, so translation ends there: Met, then Ala.
